sec: Consequences of the PCT defect in type 2 RTA · p822

items.q: Match the three arms of the PCT-defect flowchart — 1) HCO₃⁻ not reabsorbed  2) Na⁺–phosphorus exchange defect  3) Na⁺–glucose transporter inactive … A) Glycosuria  B) NAGMA  C) Loss of phosphorus
items.exp: Three arms: HCO₃⁻ not reabsorbed → NAGMA; Na⁺–phosphorus exchange defect → loss of phosphorus → rickets-like changes; Na⁺–glucose transporter inactive → glycosuria. (Book p822)

items.q: Match the cascade that follows failed HCO₃⁻ reabsorption — 1) First step  2) Next  3) Then  4) End … A) Hypokalemia  B) NAGMA  C) RAS activation  D) RTA-II: salt water wasting
items.exp: HCO₃⁻ not reabsorbed → NAGMA → RTA-II with salt water wasting → defective arteriolar volume → RAS activation → hypokalemia. (Book p822)

items.q: Loss of phosphorus in type 2 RTA produces:
items.exp: Na⁺–phosphorus exchange defect → loss of phosphorus → rickets-like changes. (Book p822)

items.q: Glycosuria in type 2 RTA results from:
opts: Loss of phosphorus from the PCT
items.exp: Na⁺–glucose transporter inactive → glycosuria (in the presence of a generalised PCT defect). (Book p822)

items.q: A child with proximal RTA has polyuria, salt craving, low blood pressure and hypokalemia on the ABG. What sequence explains it?
opts: Salt water wasting → defective arteriolar volume → RAS activation → hypokalemia
items.exp: The printed cascade for RTA-II is salt water wasting → defective arteriolar volume → RAS activation → hypokalemia. (Book p822)

items.q: ‘Salt wasting in type 2 RTA leads to RAS activation, and the resulting aldosterone effect is hypokalemia.’
opts: True — defective arteriolar volume drives RAS activation and hence hypokalemia
True, but the hypokalemia comes from the phosphate leak
False — salt wasting is seen only in distal RTA
items.exp: Defective arteriolar volume activates the RAS, and the endpoint printed in the flowchart is hypokalemia. (Book p822)

items.q: All but one of these are consequences of the generalised PCT defect. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Loss of phosphorus with rickets-like changes
NAGMA with salt and water wasting
items.exp: An alkaline urine pH belongs to distal RTA; in proximal RTA the urine pH is normal, and the printed consequences are NAGMA, phosphaturia and glycosuria. (Book p822)
